title: Accounts Basis — Working Out a Support Overage on a Building Automation Service Plan
content:
# Accounts Basis — Working Out a Support Overage on a Building Automation Service Plan

The accounts office works a support overage under the Building Automation Service Plans out as follows.

## The basis

1. **The hours it is worked out from.** The hours the overage is worked out from are the hours logged against resolved tickets in the twelve months to the handling day, taken from the plan's own history and separated by how each ticket was closed into hours closed remotely, hours closed on site and hours closed with no fault found.
2. **The included hours.** The included support hours standing to the plan's credit are the support hours the plan has been credited under its entitlement.
3. **The visit allowance.** The plan year absorbs the tier's included on-site visits, each attendance reckoned at four hours, and those hours are taken off the hours closed on site before anything else is worked out. The hours closed on site are never taken below nil by that allowance.
4. **The drawing of the included hours.** The included support hours standing to the plan's credit are then drawn against the on-site hours left after that allowance and the remote hours in the proportion each bears to the two of them together, the two of them together being taken as one hour where they fall below it; the share so drawn against the on-site hours is taken to two decimal places, and whatever of the included hours is not drawn against the on-site hours is drawn against the remote hours.
5. **The rates.** The on-site hours left after the visit allowance and the drawing are billed at the tier's on-site controls technician rate, and the remote hours left after the drawing are billed at the tier's support hour rate. Neither quantity of hours falls below nil.
6. **Hours with no fault found.** Hours logged on tickets closed with no fault found never draw the included support hours and are billed in full at the rate the remote hours carry.
7. **Hours the monitoring desk raised.** The hours logged on resolved tickets that reached the desk through the monitoring desk in those twelve months are identified separately. No uplift is charged for work the monitoring desk raised outside the tier's help desk hours.
8. **The total.** The support overage is the sum of those amounts, rounded to two decimal places.

## Worked figure on hypothetical inputs

Take a plan whose tier includes 2 on-site visits a plan year, an on-site controls technician rate of 162 USD an hour and a support hour rate of 156 USD an hour. Suppose the twelve months to the handling day carry 14 hours closed on site, 6 hours closed remotely and 2 hours closed with no fault found, and that 16 hours stand to the plan's credit.

- The visit allowance is 2 attendances reckoned at four hours each, that is 8 hours, so the on-site hours left after the allowance are 14 less 8, that is 6 hours.
- The on-site hours left and the remote hours together are 6 plus 6, that is 12 hours, which is not below one hour. The share of the 16 included hours drawn against the on-site hours is 16 multiplied by 6 divided by 12, that is 8.00 hours; but only 6 on-site hours stand to be covered, so the on-site hours billed are nil and 8.00 of the included hours were applied there, leaving 8 of the included hours for the remote hours, which likewise covers all 6 remote hours, so the remote hours billed are nil.
- The 2 hours closed with no fault found draw nothing and are billed at the rate the remote hours carry, that is 2 multiplied by 156 USD, 312.00 USD.
- The hours the monitoring desk raised carry no uplift.
- The support overage is 312.00 USD.

## A second hypothetical, with hours left to bill

On the same tier, suppose 20 hours closed on site, 10 closed remotely, none with no fault found, and 8 hours standing to the plan's credit. The allowance of 8 hours leaves 12 on-site hours; the two quantities together are 22 hours; the share drawn against the on-site hours is 8 multiplied by 12 divided by 22, that is 4.36 hours, leaving 7.64 on-site hours billed at 162 USD, that is 1237.68 USD, and the remaining 3.64 of the included hours drawn against the remote hours, leaving 6.36 remote hours billed at 156 USD, that is 992.16 USD. The support overage is 2229.84 USD.
